title: Eviction-aware slot reclamation and lightweight KV warmup for continuous batcher
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Add eviction-aware slot reclamation and best-effort KV warmup to reduce tail latency for mixed KV workloads; opt-in warmup and conservative defaults.
description: This PR adds an eviction-aware slot reclamation policy to the continuous batcher and a non-blocking background KV warmup flow. Motivation: production 99.9p latency spikes were correlated with slot reclamation that evicted recently pinned KV pages, followed by expensive KV warmups for subsequent requests. The change has two complementary parts. First, each slot now maintains a compact eviction-score moving average that captures recent pin/unpin behavior and reuse age. The allocator prefers reclaiming slots with low eviction impact. Second, when a slot fingerprint differs from an incoming request, we schedule an opportunistic background prefetch of a small number of top KV pages for that fingerprint. Prefetch is best-effort, bounded, and runs on a separate worker pool so request threads are never blocked. We also introduce a configurable soft grace window (default 25ms) that delays reuse briefly when eviction churn is detected; this reduces thrash for hot KV regions. Warmup has a per-request timeout (default 40ms) and emits metrics for warmup hits, misses, and latency delta so operators can measure benefit. Implementation highlights: changes in continuous/batcher/slot_allocator.cc and slot_metadata.h to add eviction score and reclamation heuristics; new continuous/batcher/kv_warmup.cc and kv_warmup.h for the worker queue and prefetch logic; observability changes for metrics and tracing; runtime config knobs added to runtime/config_defaults.yaml. We added unit tests and integration tests that exercise warmup behavior and a saturated-worker e2e to ensure warmup workers do not interfere with request threads. Performance results from internal benchmark runs show a reduction in 99.9p latency for mixed KV-heavy workloads when warmup is enabled with conservative defaults. The feature is feature-gated and can be disabled via runtime flags if needed. Follow-ups tracked: ENG-4097 dashboard mapping and ENG-4132 dynamic warmup tuner. The PR was squash-merged after approvals and CI green.
